title: Shrinking cutoffs and a regularizer that preserves the data
source_hypothesis: Scalar proper classical order-one P with principal tau+i f; real time-independent c in S(s,1-e,e), 0<=e<=1/4; f<=0 only on the support of a compact-base cutoff C1 equal to one near chi*c. Input H(s+(3e-1)/2) compact, chi*C*P*u and chi_minus*C*u in L2. No differentiated forcing hypothesis.
reviewed_arguments: The theorem retains the real-valued cutoff used in the preceding source proof. The printed adjacent statement does not repeat it; no unrestricted complex-cutoff completion is claimed. Every other measured-data, support, weak-order and endpoint hypothesis is retained.

The current complete metric Fefferman-Phong proof, uniform Hilbert operator bound and all-parameter quantization conversion are reused at their exact verified source bytes. An approved source citation is never substituted for the programme proof.

The full mixed ordinary/exotic calculus is derived through sufficiently long finite Weyl and conversion expansions, with cancellation of self-contractions and every differentiated remainder. All-real Sobolev and quadratic-form bounds follow by conjugation and the proved metric L2 theorem.

A nonnegative symbol cutoff is constructed from C1. Its sign region need not contain a fixed conic tube. At e<=1/4 the real quantization remainder has order -1+4e<=0, giving a leading upper bound independent of the time weight.
The regularizer is on the left of each measured operator, so the given forcing and incoming L2 norms bound the regularized ones exactly. No unassumed differentiated forcing test is used.
All symbol coefficients of the localization error vanish where the measured symbol is supported; arbitrary full remainder orders give uniform smoothing even for shrinking supports.

The outgoing term equals a nonnegative common square plus an exact symmetric operator defect. Both first Weyl corrections cancel, leaving an ordinary order-minus-two error and a controlled H(s-1) form.

The real-part commutator has full mixed error order s-1+e. The imaginary-part commutator has a purely imaginary leading symbol only for the stated real cutoff; complete adjoint and product errors have order 2s-1+3e.

Fixed positive regularization puts the solution and forcing in their actual H((3+3e)/2) and H((1+3e)/2) domains. The energy identity, fixed independent weight and Young absorption give a uniform estimate.
Fourier dominated convergence and the exact Hilbert weak-subsequence proof recover the unregularized measured solution with no additional source hypothesis.

Three solutions verify endpoint exponents, construct a shrinking positive-side cutoff without a uniform conic sign margin, and compute the nonzero affine outgoing correction exactly. Twenty-two symbolic identities passed.

All nine desktop captures, the complete original figure and two mobile samples were inspected. Two figure labels were moved off the plotted curves and the outgoing example notation was simplified; the changed captures were inspected again.

Unrestricted complex-cutoff propagation, invariant entering and oriented propagation, the arbitrary concave-index model, later sections and all remaining full-course obligations remain active. External human foundations remain explicit.
